name: Pulmonary Mechanics, Lung Compliance and Surfactant

reference.source: Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology / West's Respiratory Physiology
clinicalPearls: Inspiration is active (diaphragm and external intercostals), lowering intrapleural pressure to -8 cm H2O; quiet expiration is passive
Compliance is delta V / delta P; increased in emphysema (loss of elastic fibers), decreased in fibrosis and surfactant deficiency
Surfactant (DPPC + SP-A/B/C/D) produced by type II pneumocytes reduces surface tension, preventing alveolar collapse (Laplace law: P = 2T/r)
Airway resistance is highest in medium-sized bronchi (generations 4-8); terminal bronchioles have huge total cross-sectional area
Parasympathetic vagal M3 stimulation causes bronchoconstriction; sympathetic beta-2 stimulation mediates bronchodilation
reference.pathophysiology: Neonatal respiratory distress syndrome arises from surfactant deficiency in premature infants born before thirty-four weeks gestation. Increased surface tension promotes widespread diffuse microatelectasis, intrapulmonary right-to-left shunting, hypoxemia and hyaline membrane formation. In ARDS, inflammatory exudate neutralizes surfactant, severely reducing compliance.
additionalInvestigations: Spirometry measuring FEV1, FVC, and FEV1/FVC ratio (<0.70 defines obstructive deficit)
Body plethysmography for total lung capacity (TLC) and residual volume (RV)
Diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO)
